intro: Where the business keeps its files: your own drive, drives shared by a team, and the files that sit on invoices, staff records and other records. Share them with colleagues or with people outside, ask for files and signatures, and make documents from templates.
start: Open My Drive and upload a few files or a folder, so you see how files and their details are kept.
Make a shared drive for a team, such as Finance, and add its members.
Share a file with a colleague, then try a link for someone outside.
Ask a supplier or a customer for a document with a file request.

articles.title: Upload files and folders
articles.summary: Send files, or a whole folder, into a drive. Each one is checked before it is ready, and its details are kept.

steps.lead: Open the drive and the folder
steps.rest: where the files belong. New folder makes one here.
and choose Upload files or Upload a folder. You can also drop files onto the page.
Each file shows its progress, and you can keep working in the app while they upload.
to preview it, see its details and versions, star it, move it or make a copy.

tips: Upload a new version keeps the history: any earlier version can be restored.
Check out keeps others from changing a file while you work on it. Let go when you are done.
A file is said to be being checked until its scan is done, and blocked if something harmful was found in it.

articles.title: Share a file or folder with colleagues
articles.summary: Give a person, a group, a role, a place or everyone access, as a role you choose, for as long as you choose.

steps.lead: Open the Actions of the file or folder
steps.rest: and press Share.
a person, a group, everyone with a role, everyone at a place, or everyone in the organisation.

steps.lead: Find them and choose the role
steps.rest: they have, such as viewer or editor.

steps.lead: Set From and Until if it is for a while,
steps.rest: and tick Here only, not what is inside, to keep it to this folder alone.
They are told it was shared with them, and it shows under their Shared with me.

tips: Access given on a folder above is changed where it was given.
Shared by me lists everything you shared, and lets you stop each share.

articles.title: Share a file with someone outside the business
articles.summary: Make a link to a file or a folder, choose who may open it and for how long, and see each time it was opened.

steps.lead: Open the Actions of the file or folder
steps.rest: and press Share outside.
and give it a name, such as For the auditors.
anyone with the link, anyone with the link and its passcode, or only the people you name, who prove their address with an emailed code.
(view only, or download too), how many downloads, and when it opens and stops.
Copy the link, and the passcode if there is one. The passcode is shown once, so give it to them separately.

articles.after: Shared links lists every link you gave out. Each can be suspended, changed or revoked, and its access log says who opened it and when.
tips: A link to a folder reaches what is inside it, and nothing else.
You are told when someone opens your link, as your organisation's settings say.

articles.title: Ask someone outside for documents
articles.summary: Send a file request: each person gets their own link to upload what you asked for, and is reminded until they do.

steps.rest: on File requests, or Ask for files in the folder they should land in.

steps.lead: Say what you are asking for,
steps.rest: with guidance if it helps, and choose where the files land.
Say if it is required, which file types, how many files and how large. Ask for something else adds another.

steps.lead: Add the people you are asking,
steps.rest: by email. Ask someone else adds another.
and tick the reminders, and the emailed code if they must prove their address first.
Each person is emailed a link of their own. Save as a draft keeps it to send later.

articles.after: Open the request to see what each person sent. Accept a file, or Turn back with a note, which they are emailed.
tips: Remind those still to send reminds only the people who have not sent everything, at most once a day.
Files sent to you are checked for harmful content like any upload, and stay where they landed in Drive.

articles.title: Send a document to be signed
articles.summary: Choose the file and who signs, in order or all at once, place the signatures and send it. People outside need no account.

steps.rest: on Signatures, and find the file: a PDF, or a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file.
a member by name, or someone outside by name and email.
one after another as listed, or all at once. Set how long it waits and how often it reminds.
Put each signer's signature where it belongs, or Place a signature and date for each.
Only those whose turn it is are asked. Nothing is sent until you press it.

articles.after: Signatures shows each request as out for signature, a draft, signed, or declined, cancelled or expired, with how many have signed.

articles.title: Make a document from a template
articles.summary: Fill a letter, certificate or notice from a customer, a member of staff or another record, and file it in Drive.

steps.rest: on Drive templates, and press Generate.

steps.lead: Find the record it is filled from,
steps.rest: such as a customer or an invoice, or type what it asks for.

steps.lead: Choose Make it as and Put it in:
steps.rest: the kind of file, and the folder it is filed in.

steps.lead: Tick Ask for it to be signed once it is made
steps.rest: if it needs signatures, and say who signs.
then Generate. Choose several records to make one file for each.

tips: Those who write templates make them with New template. A template is retired, never deleted, and every change is kept as a version.

articles.title: Make a drive for a team
articles.summary: A shared drive belongs to the team, not to one person. Give it members, and their files stay when someone leaves.

steps.rest: on Shared drives.
and say what it is for.
It shows under Drives you can open.

steps.lead: Open its menu and press Members
steps.rest: to give people, groups or roles access to it.

tips: For a team or a project with its own drives, members and discussion, press New workspace. An archived workspace can still be read, but not changed.

articles.title: Get back a file you deleted
articles.summary: Files and folders put in the trash wait there for a while. Restore them, or remove them for good.

steps.rest: It shows what you put there, or a drive's trash if you choose one, with when each goes for good.
and press Restore. It goes back to its folder, or to the top of the drive if its folder is gone.

tips: A folder comes back with everything that was in it.
Remove for good is only for owners and managers of the file, and cannot be undone.
The trash empties itself after the number of days your organisation chose.

articles.title: Turn emailed documents into files
articles.summary: Give Drive an email address. Attachments sent to it land in the folder you chose, or wait for someone to file them.

steps.rest: on Drive inbox and press New inbox.

steps.lead: Give it a name and an address,
steps.rest: and choose where the mail comes from: one of your email channels, or forwarded to the app.
who may send to it, and who is told when something waits.
Mail sent to the address is listed under Waiting.
and press File them, after choosing the folder.

tips: Files are saved with the rights of whoever saved the inbox.
A message can take a minute or two to show after it is sent.
